sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Half the conference's governance claims trace to the slides
sections.para: A GRC adviser said agent governance was the subtext of The AI Conference in San Francisco. Reading the 134-session agenda and 35 slide decks traced her three failure stories to Stoica, Ameisen and Chambers, but not the poll or two case-study numbers. Policy enforced outside the model was the loudest idea, and the best fact-check sat in speaker notes.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Three items trace, three do not; policy-outside-model dominated
sections.para: Stoica's gamed benchmark, Ameisen's hidden concealment signals and Chambers' green dashboard trace to the stage; the 43% poll, 1,200 developers and 1,500 agents do not. Five companies said policy must sit outside the model, silent failure was the commonest story, Monday.com reports 56% of production pull requests without human comment, and one speaker flagged her own unverified numbers.

sections.label: How we read it
sections.line: Decks, notes and abstracts were read, not transcripts
sections.para: The conference ran at Pier 48 from 29 September to 1 October 2026, with 134 sessions and about 160 speakers. Of 36 published decks, 35 were read with speaker notes; no transcripts were available, so quotes come from decks, notes and abstracts. The starting point was Angela Polania's post and recap for Elevate Consult.

sections.label: Six items, traced
sections.line: Three stories trace to keynotes; three numbers do not
sections.para: The gamed key-value benchmark is Ion Stoica's, concealment invisible in output is Emmanuel Ameisen's, and the green dashboard is Mike Chambers', echoed by Datadog's 200 OK. No source was found for the 43% poll or the 1,200 developers. The 1,500-agent registry architecture matches PayPal's abstract, which gives no count.

sections.label: What the programme kept saying
sections.line: Speakers kept saying policy must be enforced outside models
sections.para: Hedera, Dropbox, C1, ReFocus and SS&C all insisted on deterministic enforcement outside the model, and NEAR called prompt injection an authority problem. The worst failures succeed quietly and wrongly. Speakers stressed naming an owner for every agent, warned that evaluations get gamed, and Microsoft noted that discovery accelerated while validation and remediation did not.

sections.label: Where the talks disagree
sections.line: Talks split on humans, rules, inventories, probes, open models
sections.para: Rubrik called human-in-the-loop dead while others kept approvals; RSA's answer is that humans approve the entry, not the journey. Models can flag but rules should gate. Delinea's thirteen spawned agents defeat inventories unless registries hold mandates. Probes and output monitors are both just monitors, and Faros's open-model comparison rests partly on only 29 tasks.

sections.label: Observations
sections.line: Nobody showed the policy, and review is thinning
sections.para: Speakers described policy outside the model but none published the actual policy file. Monday.com's notes say 56% of production pull requests get no human comment. Camila Maia's notes flagged her AT&T figures as unverified and dropped a Pinterest figure. Claims from CData, Navan, Stoica, Goodfire and Norvig are checkable, but remain claims until run.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: No transcripts, and not found does not mean false
sections.para: Quotes come from decks, notes and abstracts, and stage remarks may differ. The three untraced items may have been said live. The six items were one reader's choice from 134 sessions, and only a third published material. Most figures are vendors' own, the readings are the site's, and speakers can correct them via agent@riskmandate.ai.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: the agenda, recordings, decks and Polania's recap
sections.para: Researched by the site's agent from material read on 16 October 2026: the aiconference.com agenda and recordings, Angela Polania's Elevate Consult recap of 2 October 2026, talks by Stoica, Ameisen, Chambers, Walker, Tyler, Polosukhin, Kiely and Norvig, and decks from Datadog, ReFocus AI, Microsoft, Faros, Latitude.sh, CData and Navan, plus agenda abstracts.
